finding.statement: The Hertfordshire baptism index records twelve children baptised at Great Berkhamsted to a father John Gurney between 1597 and 1637 - Hugh 1597, Anne 1599, Amye 1602, Bridgett 1606, Henrye 1610, Sara 1615, Jhon 1624, Richard 1626, Elizabeth 1629, Michaell 1631, Sarah 1634 and Francys/Francis 1636/7 - with the mother not indexed in any row. The run is forty years long, which is not one man. The parish's burial record, read across seven surname stems rather than one, holds sixteen Gurney-variant burials between 1579 and 1643, among them Jhon Gourney in 1612 and again in 1620; no John Gurney-variant burial occurs at Berkhamsted after 1620, and none anywhere in Hertfordshire between 1620 and 1690 except Jonathan Gurney at Bovingdon in 1682-3. That post-1620 absence is not interpretable as departure, because the record set states that many Hertfordshire registers are defective for 1643-1660 and the parish's Gurney burials stop in 1643 and resume only in 1711.

finding.statement: Candidate C is two men, and only the elder is eliminated. Searched by parent rather than by child, the Great Berkhamsted baptisms to a father John Gurney run from 1597 to 1637 — forty years, which is not one man. The natural break is the nine-year gap between Sara 1615 and Jhon 1624, and a Jhon Gourney was buried in the parish in 1620, between the two. C(i), fathering from 1597, was born about 1570-75, twenty-five to thirty years before the colonial John, and is eliminated on age — a ground immune to the same-name problem. C(ii), fathering from 1624, was born about 1598-1602, so about 51 in 1653, the best documented age fit in the whole field; he carries three colonial forenames, which no other English household reaches. What holds him at a low probability is that his household stopped because his children were dying rather than because he left: of the parish's sixteen Gurney-variant burials between 1579 and 1643, five fall between November 1637 and March 1638/9, and two of them match to the day the recorded death dates of two of his own children. Three further constraints run against him — no Mary Gurney is baptised in the parish at any date between 1544 and 1888; no John Gurney marriage occurs anywhere in Hertfordshire between 1600 and 1654, so his wife cannot be named or tested against a Mary; and a Richard Gurney buried on 28 June 1638 would collapse the candidate outright if he is C(ii)'s son of 1626, though the parish held four contemporaneous Gurney households and the index cannot tell them apart.
